name: kalimba_hook
description: African thumb piano (kalimba / mbira) carrying the hook first and the high sparkle later.
character: A thumb piano played close and dry: a bright, short-decay pluck that states the hook first, clear enough in the 500 Hz to 4 kHz band that a phone speaker returns every note.
sources: KB african (mbira and thumb pianos: a halo of high-frequency buzz around each note; the SoundFont kalimba has none: ESTIMATE, not modelled)
KB short-form-functional-music (the hook starts inside 3 s on the instrument with the clearest attack: starting value)
ESTIMATE: azimuth, distance, level and EQ are starting values for this piece, not measured
STARTING VALUE: onset_fade_ms 10: several strokes land together on every strong beat and their sharp starts add into one impulse the click row flags; a soft attack is also what "smooth" asks for

MEASURED: the mastered file had click events at the onsets of overlapping notes, where the sampler tick lands on a still-ringing note and soften_onsets leaves it alone by design; STARTING VALUE: low-pass at 6000 Hz, above what a phone speaker returns

STARTING VALUE: low-pass at 4.5 kHz: a phone speaker returns little above about 5 kHz (KB short-form-functional-music), and the sharp edges of plucked and struck onsets above it are what the click row reacts to
